items.defectStatement: When neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar, evt.destinationCalendar is null and the optional push discards the collective hosts’ destination calendars. Their configured calendars therefore never reach event creation.
obligations: Include team destination calendars even when evt.destinationCalendar is null.
Preserve any existing destination calendar before the appended team calendars.
Keep the change restricted to collective team events.
items.notes: The closing brace is outside the replacement. Initializing the array before pushing is also valid.

items.defectStatement: Google updateEvent searches destination calendars for the absent externalCalendarId instead of falling back to the first configured destination. This passes an undefined calendarId to update and its follow-up patch, preventing updates to the configured calendar.
obligations: Preserve an explicitly supplied, nonempty externalCalendarId.
Use the main host destination’s externalId when externalCalendarId is absent.
Handle an empty or null destinationCalendar without throwing.
items.notes: Scoped to the finding’s updateEvent defect. The gold also mentions the analogous deleteEvent defect, which requires a separate edit. Unlike deleteEvent, updateEvent has no explicit primary fallback.

items.defectStatement: EventManager.create dereferences the first destination calendar without checking whether it exists. A Google Meet booking with a null or empty destinationCalendar throws instead of selecting the Cal Video fallback.
obligations: Allow null, undefined, and empty destination-calendar collections without throwing.
Select Cal Video for Meet when the first destination is absent or is not Google Calendar.
Preserve Meet for a Google Calendar destination and preserve unrelated locations.
items.notes: The fallback assignment and closing brace remain outside the replacement.

items.defectStatement: Organization creation sets slug when team billing is enabled instead of disabled. Billing-enabled organizations receive both slug and requestedSlug prematurely, while billing-disabled organizations receive neither.
obligations: Set the organization slug directly when team billing is disabled.
When billing is enabled, store requestedSlug without setting slug directly.
Preserve the remaining organization metadata.
items.notes: Only the slug condition needs inversion.

items.defectStatement: Recurring cancellation ignores the current reference’s resolved credential and deletes each occurrence’s first calendar reference through the organizer’s credentials. This repeats organizer deletions and leaves co-host calendar events undeleted.
obligations: Use the current reference’s resolved credential, including credentials loaded from the database.
Select each occurrence’s calendar reference by the current credential rather than taking its first calendar reference.
Delete using the selected occurrence reference’s uid and externalCalendarId.
Preserve awaiting and error handling for the deletion promises.
items.notes: The replacement deliberately leaves the existing push, closing blocks, and Promise.all intact. It addresses the credential-bearing collective references described by the finding.

items.defectStatement: EventManager.create drops credentialId from video booking references by assigning undefined to every non-calendar result. Cancellation requires that credentialId to locate the video credential, so those meetings are not deleted.
obligations: Preserve result.credentialId for video references.
Continue using result.credentialId for calendar references.
Keep externalCalendarId restricted to calendar references.
items.exampleFix:
externalCalendarId: isCalendarType ? result.externalId : undefined,
        credentialId: result.credentialId,
items.notes: No destination-calendar credential fallback is needed.

items.defectStatement: Office365 createEvent always targets the first destination calendar, regardless of which host’s credential authenticates the request. A collective co-host’s token therefore targets the organizer’s calendar instead of the co-host’s configured calendar, potentially failing creation.
obligations: Make the invoking credential’s ID available to Office365 createEvent.
Select the destination associated with that credential instead of the first destination.
Preserve the default-calendar endpoint when no applicable destination externalId exists.
items.notes: The createEvent signature at line 72 is outside the anchor and must accept credentialId, or equivalent credential state must be added elsewhere. An arguments-based workaround is incompatible with this package’s ES5-targeted async TypeScript. The gold’s analogous Lark defect is outside this finding.

items.defectStatement: The recurring deletion block runs inside the calendar-reference loop but scans all organizer calendar credentials on every iteration. It repeatedly deletes each occurrence’s first calendar event and fails to delete co-host events through their own credentials.
obligations: Scope each outer reference’s recurring deletions to its resolved credential.
Match each occurrence’s calendar reference to that credential.
Use each matched reference’s uid and externalCalendarId without repeating organizer deletions for other hosts.
Preserve the recurrence guard, promise error handling, and single-booking path.
items.notes: Overlaps #13. Moving the bulk operation outside the outer loop is another approach, but scoping it to the current credential fits this anchor.

items.defectStatement: Google createEvent applies the primary-calendar fallback only to insertion, leaving selectedCalendar undefined when no destination matches the credential. The subsequent hangout-link patch uses that undefined value and fails to update the event description.
obligations: Resolve selectedCalendar to primary when no matching destination externalId exists.
Use the same resolved calendar ID for insertion and the follow-up patch.
Preserve credential-specific destination selection when a match exists.
items.notes: Resolving the shared variable fixes the later patch without editing its call site.
